Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. The position is located at United States Army Dugway Proving Ground, approximately 50 minutes from Tooele, Utah, and 90 minute drive from Salt Lake City, Utah. Dugway offers various alternate work schedule opportunities with most of the workforce working 4 ten-hour shifts Monday through Thursday. Employees choosing to live off post may use subsidized commuter van transport which operates to and from many of the major cities and towns throughout Utah. Contact the Relocation Program Manager at 435-831-2260. For more information about Dugway's beautiful terrain and community go to our website http://www.dugway.army.mil.
MajorDuties: Manages and implements the Garrison Energy Program.
Develops local policy local policy and directives to reduce energy cost and to support stewardship of resources, readiness, and sustainability.
Provides professional engineering services to other organizations on energy/water conservation matters
Conducts studies in research, data management, trend analysis, and special projects in all phases of the Garrison?s energy management program.
Plans and coordinates work on energy and utilities related matters with other engineers and subordinate personnel

Operates computer-aided design and drafting equipment and personal computer equipment in the development of plans and specifications, to generate or revise drawings, edit specifications, and perform general engineering computations.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Details.Education: Required for GS-09 level: To qualify based on your work experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which includes experience professional engineering work in an energy program with the goal of assisting in developing policy and efficiencies to reduce an organizations/installations energy costs; and Assisting higher grade engineers involved in improving energy efficiency. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education Substitution for Specialized Experience for GS-09 level: Successful completion of at least a Master's or equivalent graduate degree, or two full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree. OR Combination Experience & Education Substitution for Specialized Experience for GS-09 level: If you have some, but not all, of the experience or education described above, you may still qualify by combining the amount of creditable experience and education that you possess. To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of graduate education in excess of 18 hours (total semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100% to qualify. Required for GS-11 level: To qualify based on your work experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which includes experience performing professional engineering work implementing an energy program with the goal of developing policy and efficiencies to reduce an organizations/installations energy cost and to support stewardship of resources, readiness, and sustainability. Advised an organization/installation leadership on ways to save energy and to evaluate the energy program. Participates in energy awareness throughout the Installation. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education Substitution for Specialized Experience for GS-11 level: Successful completion of a PhD or equivalent graduate degree, if related to this position. OR Combination of Education & Experience for GS-11 level: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Required for GS-12 level: To qualify based on your work experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which includes experience performing professional engineering work managing and implementing an energy program with the goal of developing policy and efficiencies to reduce an organizations/installations energy cost and to support stewardship of resources, readiness, and sustainability. Advised an organization/installation leadership on ways to save energy and to evaluate the energy program. Participates in energy awareness throughout the Installation. Represents an organization/installations at symposiums, conferences, and meetings. Conducts studies in research, data management, trend analysis, and special projects in all phases of the Army energy management program. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11) FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, The incumbent will be responsible for managing and/or oversees approved fundamental biological research projects and related advanced technology developments in support of the overall RDCX- Advanced Research Division (CXR) mission.
Details.SubAgencyName: Research and Development Directorate (RD)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a BIOLOGIST at the GS-0401-13/14 some of your typical work assignments may include: These projects advance biological research and development activities which provide long-range R&D, coupled with systems engineering, to realize and deliver breakthrough, unimagined capabilities and technologies that combat emerging WMD threats as well as support Over-the-Horizon Arms Control (OTHAC) and Information Resilience. Proposes, implements, and evaluates innovative biological research concepts and activities directed at improving the ultimate effectiveness, efficiency, usability, suitability, and/or affordability of counter-WMD capabilities. Researches and utilizes the principles and employment of scientific processes and capabilities to design and deliver unimagined capabilities to the warfighter and within the offensive WMD capability mission area. Provides expert guidance on adversary threats and countermeasures to lead effective planning and create affordable investments in the research, development, and innovation of future capabilities to counter emerging WMD/CBRNE threats. Incumbent serves as an expert source of and provides guidance regarding biological science and technology information in the counter-WMD/CBRNE fields dealing with capabilities and issues in such areas as international conflict and war, strategic and tactical weapon systems; domestic and international terrorism; national and military intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance; net-centric warfare; counter-proliferation, non-proliferation, and arms control; and counterterrorism. Formulates overall project objectives; recommends resource allocations among stakeholders, partners and collaborators to best meet program objectives; provides necessary documentation, justification, and procurement information for resource awards; establishes task priorities and major milestones for decisions, deliverables, and acceptance criteria; monitors progress of individual projects and performers; and assesses and reports on program risks, issues, and opportunities. Evaluates white papers and full proposals submitted to the Agency for funding consideration when solicited through request for proposals, broad agency announcements or other transactional authorities. Makes technical decisions with regard to approved project directions, modifies plans and milestones as appropriate, and makes necessary adjustments among and within research tasks to optimize project productivity as measured in terms of the technical viability of options and/or technology readiness level of deliverables for integration with, or transition to, other RDCX, CXR, Agency, and DoD efforts. Analyzes complex project variables to include manpower, supply, budget, and travel resources and develops recommendations to resolve substantive problems of the effectiveness and efficiency of program work operations. Develops solutions to get projects back on track when obstacles occur such as continuing resolutions, budget cuts, contract delays, etc. The incumbent participates with higher-graded staff members in establishing goals and organizing and defending biological research and development programs spanning the DoD's 6.1 (basic research), 6.2 (applied research) and 6.3 (advanced technology development) funding categories. Serves as Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to assist the Contracting Officer in pre-award and post-award activities as defined by the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement. Establishes and maintains contacts with appropriate scientists and engineers at Department of Energy (DOE) laboratories, DoD warfare and Research & Engineering Centers, Federal research funding agencies, universities, and industry. Researches and provides biological science and technology information in the weapons of mass destruction field. Interacts with Agency research customers and senior officials in the DoD and other offices to participate in the coordination, evaluation, integration, and facilitation of transition of science and technology products. Communicates scientific concepts into clearly understood options and opportunities for senior Agency and DoD management officials. Participates in DTRA, DoD, Federal and other activities to gain understanding of Agency, DoD, and national science and technology needs and requirements. Participates in working groups, DoD Technology Panels, war games, roundtables, DDR&E's Technology Area Plans (TAP), and other groups that address Agency, DoD, and national science and technology needs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for a Environmental Engineer: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. Basic Requirement for a Physical Scientist: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to one of the majors, as shown in A above, that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience GS-11: One year of specialized experience which includes experience identifying methods to minimize waste generation; developing environmental strategies to reduce contaminations; performing environmental research to prepare research reports; and providing guidance on environmental compliance and pollution prevention. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience GS-12: One year of specialized experience which includes experience using environmental or engineering practices for hazardous/regulated waste management and/or hazardous waste characterization; reviewing plans and specification for environmental compliance; preparing reports on environmental quality programs; and providing guidance on environmental matters for projects. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11 or above). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

Fort Bragg is co-located with Fayetteville, a culturally diverse city. Fort Bragg is known as the "Home of the Airborne and Special Operations Forces".

Conducts surveys and proposes types of plant materials, which will best meet the needs of particular conservation projects.
Interacts with public health officials for the control of insect and rodent disease vectors.

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirements: The Natural Resources Specialist occupation has specific educational requirements which apply to all positions. You must have completed a full four year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or a discipline related to the position. OR You must have an appropriate combination of education and experience. Your education must include courses equivalent to a major field of study in any of the acceptable fields listed above. (The number of semester hours required to constitute a major field of study is the amount specified by the college or university attended; if this number can not be obtained from the college or university, 24 semester hours will be considered equivalent). The quality of the combination of experience and education is sufficient to demonstrate the skills and abilities to perform progressively more responsible work in this occupation. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which prepared you to do the work in this job. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position, you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized experience is defined as: Advising on matters concerning natural resources conservation (e.g. wild land fire, forestry, weed management, watershed management, erosion control, ecosystem protection, wetlands management and land reclamation); coordinating with local, state and federal agencies regarding natural resources management and conservation issues; ensuring projects are in compliance with applicable laws and regulations; and briefing higher level management on natural resources program status and initiatives. To qualify at the GS 07 Level: Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service which includes One year of specialized experience which includes demonstrated experience; 1) Ensure proper collection and preservation of specimens;. 2) Independently perform recurring, well-precedented projects using standard methods and techniques 3) Calculate and correlate test results. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: I have successfully completed one full academic year of graduate-level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as, biological sciences, natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have some graduate education as described in B, but less than the required one year. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% . (The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) To qualify at the GS 9 Level: Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes demonstrated experience such Applying developing and implementing multiple-use resource management plans covering diverse resource management issues. 2 Assess the environmental impact of various practices. 3) apply environmental regulatory requirements in resource management reviews and contract proposals. OR Education: I have successfully completed a masters or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B or J.D. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have some graduate education as described in B, but less than the required one year. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% . (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) To qualify at the GS 11 Level: Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service which includes demonstrated experience preparing environmental, natural resource and/or wildland fire technical reports. Preparing statements of work for wildland fire, environmental, natural resources and/or project tasks. OR Education: I have successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as biological sciences, natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have at least two years of graduate education as described in B, but less than the required three years. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% .(Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirements: The Natural Resources Specialist occupation has specific educational requirements which apply to all positions. You must have completed a full four year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major field of study in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or a discipline related to the position. OR You must have an appropriate combination of education and experience. Your education must include courses equivalent to a major field of study in any of the acceptable fields listed above. (The number of semester hours required to constitute a major field of study is the amount specified by the college or university attended; if this number can not be obtained from the college or university, 24 semester hours will be considered equivalent). The quality of the combination of experience and education is sufficient to demonstrate the skills and abilities to perform progressively more responsible work in this occupation. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which prepared you to do the work in this job. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position, you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized experience is defined as: Advising on matters concerning natural resources conservation (e.g. wild land fire, forestry, weed management, watershed management, erosion control, ecosystem protection, wetlands management and land reclamation); coordinating with local, state and federal agencies regarding natural resources management and conservation issues; ensuring projects are in compliance with applicable laws and regulations; and briefing higher level management on natural resources program status and initiatives. To qualify at the GS 07 Level: Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service which includes One year of specialized experience which includes demonstrated experience; 1) Ensure proper collection and preservation of specimens;. 2) Independently perform recurring, well-precedented projects using standard methods and techniques 3) Calculate and correlate test results. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: I have successfully completed one full academic year of graduate-level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as, biological sciences, natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts. OR Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have some graduate education as described in B, but less than the required one year. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) To qualify at the GS 9 Level:Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes demonstrated experience such Applying developing and implementing multiple-use resource management plans covering diverse resource management issues. 2 Assess the environmental impact of various practices. 3) apply environmental regulatory requirements in resource management reviews and contract proposals. OR Education: I have successfully completed a masters or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B or J.D. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have some graduate education as described in B, but less than the required one year. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) To qualify at the GS 11 Level: Specialized Experience: I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service which includes demonstrated experience preparing environmental, natural resource and/or wildland fire technical reports. Preparing statements of work for wildland fire, environmental, natural resources and/or project tasks. OR Education: I have successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as biological sciences, natural resources management, etc. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) Combination of Education and Experience: I have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have at least two years of graduate education as described in B, but less than the required three years. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.)

The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serve as the DPW staff specialist in wild land in order to provide technical advice and guidance to protect life, property, endangered species, and other natural resource values at risk.
Integrate wildfire and prescribed fire programs at the strategic, operational, and tactical levels.
Focus on biological surveys, monitoring, and research in orders to project level execution of the wildlife, wetland, invasive species, and forestry management programs as detailed various plans.
Maintains effective working relationships with a variety of teams, agencies, and organizations.
Participate in the NEPA process by analyzing potential impacts in order to assist with mitigation strategies and alternatives for natural resource wildland fire related projects.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement: This position has a basic entry requirement. The entry requirement requires completion of education or a combination of education and experience sufficient to be comparable to that normally acquired through the completion of a four-year course of study with a major in the professional or scientific field. Please refer to the following sites for all possible ways to meet the Basic Requirements for this position: Landscape Architecture Series 0807 - Landscape Architecture Series 0807 (opm.gov) Architecture Series 0808 - Architecture Series 0808 (opm.gov) All Professional Engineering Positions 0800 -all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf (opm.gov) In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Your resume must describe at least one year of specialized experience which prepared you to do the work in this job. Specialized Experience GS-7: One year of experience which includes assisting with basic quality assurance; providing support in completing engineering and/or architectural projects. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the Federal service (GS-05) OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Superior Academic Achievement: In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:(1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR(2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR(3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience GS-9: One year of experience which includes assisting in conducting investigations and site visits to develop solutions to problems related to design and site conditions encountered during construction. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the Federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: landscape architect, architect, or engineering-civil, environmental, mechanical, or electrical. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience GS-11: One year of experience which includes applying field engineering practices by coordinating construction operations and assisting with contract interpretations, scheduling, and safety in the field. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the Federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as those indicated above under Basic Education. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience GS-12: One year of experience which includes applying filed engineering practices to oversee construction operations to ensure contract interpretations, and construction methods and schedules. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the Federal service (GS-11). For the GS-12 level, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted. This position has selective placement factor for the GS-12 level, which must be met prior to employment and for continued employment. Selective Placement Factor at the GS-12: This position requires registration as a professional engineer, professional architect and/or professional landscape architect at the time of application. (You must provide a copy of your professional registration at the time of application.)

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is one of the best! In 2020, USACE ranked #2 of government large-agency subcomponent! USACE is one of the world's premier public engineering, design, and construction management agencies. We serve the American people, striving to provide the most effective engineering and environmental science solutions to the nation's complex problems affecting national security, the economy and the environment in which we live. USACE offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment, providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. We rely on leaders with vision, creativity, and programmatic and technical expertise to lead us into the future. Align your talents with your passion and find out why the U. S. As a Team Leader or Project Engineer, provides technical assistance and work direction to a quality assurance team of engineers and/or technical personnel responsible for thorough implementation of the government Quality Assurance (QA) Program.

Perform planning, design, construction and operation tasks in accordance with District Project Management Business Process (PMBP) matrices for milcon, environmental and civil works projects and Construction-Operations Division SOPs.
Perform investigations and site visits to develop solutions to problems related to design and differing site conditions encountered during construction.

Obtains safety requirements of the contract and the Resident office safety goals through implementation of the government Safety Program and insuring effective development and implementation of the contractor's Safety Program.

For GS-9 Specialized Experience: Have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes the following. Perform a variety of development tasks for subjects such as hazardous waste (HW) management, disposal and safe drinking water. Research and provide information for current environmental laws, regulations, and policies for things such as Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Clean Water Act (CWA), Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) and the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). Use Federal, state and local laws and regulations related to environmental protection issues. OR Have successfully completed a Master's degree or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree, or completion of all requirements for an LL.B or J.D. degree from an accredited college or university. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have at least two years of graduate education as described in B, but less than the required three years. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) For GS-11 Specialized Experience: Have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service which includes the following. Support the organization through planning, directing, coordinating, monitoring, evaluating and providing technical guidance for the installation's environmental protection programs. Perform environmental inspections and assist in the correction of inspection findings and proposes actions to resolve deficiencies. OR Have successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as Physical Sciences, Personnel Administration, Human Resources Management, Business Administration. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Have the specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have at least two years of graduate education as described in B, but less than the required three years. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.)

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Irwin is a world class training center for America's Soldiers, known for its excellent desert training and vast recreational opportunities. Located 37 miles NE of Barstow, CA, in the Mojave Desert midway between Las Vegas, NV and Los Angeles, CA. Nearest airports are in Ontario, CA (120 miles), Los Angeles (175 miles) and Las Vegas (180 miles). Fort Irwin has a mass bus system that travels to and from Barstow (37 miles) and Victorville (69 miles). Victorville is the business hub and draws consumers from beyond its area. For information on these cities, visit their websites; http://www.barstowca.org/; http://www.losangeles.com/; http://ci.victorville.ca.us/; https://www.ontarioca.gov/; http:// www.lasvegasnevada.gov/ Fort Irwin is one of the 4th highest paying federal installations, falling under the Los Angeles-Long Beach, CA locality at 32.41%.
MajorDuties: Analyze and interpret environmental policy directives to develop, modify, and implement water conservation and plans and practices to meet objectives while maintaining continuity of work.

Identify, research and recommend solutions to problems encountered in achieving/maintaining compliance with Federal, state and local laws and regulations such as RCRA, CAA, CWA, SDWA, and TSCA issues.

Interpret and implement new or revised policy directives or program materials of higher authority or regulatory agencies, establishing plans for use by installation, tenant and reserve component activities.
Provide support to the restoration and remediation program, identifying issues and developing resolution methods and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations.

Provide scientific, engineering, statistical analysis and forecasting to develop, review and implement environmental standards, specifications, and operating procedures allowing others to execute compliance oversite.

Details.SubAgencyName: OFFICE OF THE GARRISON COMMANDER
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Provides industrial engineering services and technical assistance for increasing the productivity of the Directorate of Public Work's engineering work force.
Conducts research, compiles data, and prepares charts for Review and Analysis briefings and Installation Status Reports.
Analyzes changes and trends in overall DPW workload, workload distribution and similar factors relating to Stationing Actions, , etc.
Applies professional knowledge in the areas of systems engineering, workload analysis and forecasting, cost analysis, and economic analysis.
Manages the operation of the General Fund Enterprise Business Systems (GFEBS) and Geographic Information System (GIS) including data entry, updates, data quality assurance and data analysis.
Serves as the DPW Security Officer and OPSEC Officer.
Serves as the DPW central point of contact and subject matter expert for government and contractor issues on Integrated Facilities System (IFS)

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens The primary objective of this DHA is to appoint qualified candidates who are not existing DoD competitive service employees with permanent status. Category rating, veteran's preference, military spouse preference, and traditional rating and ranking of applicants are not applicable to this this vacancy. Applications will be reviewed and referred for selection on 16th February 2023; and again, at closing date on 3rd March, 2023. This announcement will be closed when a selection has been made. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Natural Resources Specialist 1. Degree: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR 2. Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. (NOTE: You MUST submit your college transcripts with your application package.) In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1). Administer various natural resources programs to ensure compliance with natural resources laws and regulations; 2). Utilize automatic data processing systems including microcomputers and a Geographic Information System to store and retrieve data to meet program needs; 3). Prepare long term work plans and budgets, and track spending obligations; 4). Develop and administer contracts and/or hold and use a government purchase card for funds regarding control of invasive species, outdoor recreation, or other natural resources needs. OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. (NOTE: You MUST submit your college transcripts with your application package.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Natural Resources Specialist (Ranger): Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: For GS-05: Applicants who meet the basic requirements are fully qualified for the GS-05 grade level.Bachelor Degree: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience applying basic knowledge of biological practices, principles and techniques in a natural resource management environment, or additional education. For GS-07: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: Using biological practices principles and techniques sufficient to assist in the recommendations of planning and implementing environmental, recreational, and natural resource management activities at a water resources project. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:(1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses. OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum. OR (3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. For GS-09: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: Using biological practices, principles, and techniques sufficient to assist in the recommendations of planning and implementing environmental, recreational, and natural resource management activities at a water resources project. Experience in natural resource management and related laws, policies, and regulations as it pertains to biodiversity, threatened and endangered species, wetland protection, cultural resources, and agricultural lease program. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is one of the best! In 2020, USACE ranked #2 of government large-agency subcomponent! USACE is one of the world's premier public engineering, design, and construction management agencies. We serve the American people, striving to provide the most effective engineering and environmental science solutions to the nation's complex problems affecting national security, the economy and the environment in which we live. USACE offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. Develop plans for facility improvements which are consistent with current and future demands.
Enforce a public safety program for the project, which includes surveillance, and maintenance of buoys, signs, and fences.
Assist in developing and implementing specific land use plans for the project.
Participate in the development of various planning documents, including Master Plans and Operational Management Plans (OMP), for management of the project's man-made and natural resources.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Civilian Employees of the Organization Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Interchange Agreement Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Natural Resources Specialist (Ranger): Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: For GS-05: Applicants who meet the basic requirements are fully qualified for the GS-05 grade level. Bachelor Degree: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience applying basic knowledge of biological practices, principles and techniques in a natural resource management environment, or additional education. For GS-07: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: Using biological practices principles and techniques sufficient to assist in the recommendations of planning and implementing environmental, recreational, and natural resource management activities at a water resources project. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:(1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses. OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum. OR (3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. For GS-09: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: Using biological practices, principles, and techniques sufficient to assist in the recommendations of planning and implementing environmental, recreational, and natural resource management activities at a water resources project. Experience in natural resource management and related laws, policies, and regulations as it pertains to biodiversity, threatened and endangered species, wetland protection, cultural resources, and agricultural lease program. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Contract Administration Environmental Planning Environmental Stewardship and Advocacy Natural Resource Management Public Planning Security Program Management Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent. For GS-05 - must have 52 weeks of Federal service to at least GS-04. For GS-07 - must have 52 weeks of Federal service to at least GS-05. For GS-09 - must have 52 weeks of Federal service to at least GS-07.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 5 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: This position is located in the Environmental Management function at ARNG base. Serves as a program manager within the Environmental Bureau, providing expert technical advice directly to the Environmental Program Manager. This position will ensure compliance with policies, regulations, and federal, state, and local statues. Serves as the program manager for the Environmental Performance Assessment System (EPAS) program, ensuring MTARNG units, tenants, supply personnel and facility managers are in compliance with a variety of regulations, monitoring and measuring through audits, and providing corrective actions when necessary. Such environmental programs that will be regularly reviewed for compliance include: air monitoring, water permitting, Installation Compatible Use Zone (ICUZ), installation specific hazardous material and solid waste plan, installation specific Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasures (SPCC) Plans, mitigation requirements associated with implementation of National environmental Policy Act (NEPA) actions, installation specific underground storage tank SOPs, etc. Position will be required to read and understand regulatory and SOP details, audit a variety of programs managed by the MTARNG, write concise non-compliance findings, and assist in implementing corrective actions, if necessary. Position will be responsible to conduct surveys, inspections, and evaluates activities to identify and initiate corrective actions for environmental deficiencies. Develops and/or reviews regulations and directives and management plans required to establish an environmental program that complies with federal, state, and local regulations. Uses agency directives as broad policy in developing these regulations. Reviews, initiates corrective action, coordinates with NGB on all environmental reporting requirements, including EQuip Survey Tool, WEBCASS and CSI. Position will create and manage federal funding via STEP program, working with other program managers to ensure project develop is complete and funding is adequate. Will manage annual federal funds, seeking reimbursement via state Master Cooperative Agreement, ensuring funding is reimbursed accurately and in a timely manner. Coordinates ARNG level facility environmental plans, programs and projects. Serves as point of contact for training units, developing project descriptions and analyzing potential effects, if necessary. Works in cooperation with other Environmental Bureau program managers, providing assistance for programs such as NEPA and SPCC. Position has to the potential to review proposed construction and operation and maintenance plans, providing sound environmental review that will ensure the project meets regulatory requirements. May serve as the ARNG contact and spokesperson with local, federal and state regulators, when necessary. May serve as the department contact person for various NGB departments and programs, providing accurate reporting to NGB when requested.
Details.Evaluations: Once the announcement has closed, your resume and supporting documentation will be used to determine if you meet the qualifications listed on this announcement. If you are minimally qualified, your resume and supporting documentation will be compared to your responses on the assessment questionnaire to determine your level of experience. If you rate yourself higher than is supported by your application package, your responses may be adjusted and/or you may be excluded from consideration for this position. If you are found to be among the top qualified candidates, you will be referred to the selecting official for employment consideration. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities and other characteristics): General knowledge of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).Knowledge of federal, state and local laws and regulations. Ability to initiate, develop and execute environmental activities and development of organizational guidance. Ability to review plans, specification designs, etc. prepared for the purpose of conformance with environmental standards. Ability to prepare technical documents, as required, with clear and concise information. Ability to write audit findings for deficiencies against federal, state, and local regulations. Ability to express in writing, deficiencies, and implement corrective actions. Ability to analyze situations, develop solutions and implement programs. Ability to communicate verbally with both civilian and military entities. Skills include ability to work independently, provide creative problem-solving when necessary, and work open-minded. Skills include ability to manage multiple databases, keeping accurate documentation and provide analysis when necessary. Ability to review environmental data, when needed, and provide analysis or address data inaccuracies.

MajorDuties: You will undertake analysis and prepare documentation for studies related to major water resource projects and other special studies assigned in the district.
You will develop, in coordination with project manager and interdisciplinary project delivery team, cost estimate and determines resource requirements for accomplishing work.

You will assist in the identification of water resource problems, inventorying and forecasting conditions, formulation of solutions to address problems and evaluate and compare solutions to determine the best plan to address water resource issues.
You will prepare written reports or sections of reports detailing study results, conclusions and recommendations.
You will ensure adherence to applicable statutes, policies and regulations which pertain to federal decision making related to water resources development projects.

OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Community Planner, Landscape Architect, Wildlife Biologist, Biologist, Ecologist, Archaeologist, Geographer. OR Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on:(1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR(3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. For GS-09: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes preparation of feasibility level water resource studies which may involve navigation or flood control and/or other water resource development activities. This experience includes assisting in the scoping of data collection and analysis to understand the effects of alternative plans to support water resources planning reports and decision documents. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Community Planner, Landscape Architect, Wildlife Biologist, Biologist, Ecologist, Archaeologist, Geographer. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. MajorDuties: You will undertake analysis and prepare documentation for studies related to major water resource projects and other special studies assigned in the district.
You will develop, in coordination with project manager and interdisciplinary project delivery team, cost estimate and determines resource requirements for accomplishing work.

You will assist in the identification of water resource problems, inventorying and forecasting conditions, formulation of solutions to address problems and evaluate and compare solutions to determine the best plan to address water resource issues.
You will prepare written reports or sections of reports detailing study results, conclusions and recommendations.
You will ensure adherence to applicable statutes, policies and regulations which pertain to federal decision making related to water resources development projects.
